journal: Anal. Chem. 67 (14), 2368-2372; Jackson, Bowman, Fulton: Water Solubility Measurements in Supercritical Fluids and High-Pressure Liquids Using Near-Infrared Spectroscopy
needs_pass2_reason: text layer was clean and every cell matched the page image
experimental_method: Water is injected into a 5 cm path-length high-pressure near-IR transmission cell (sapphire windows, stirred) filled with the fluid; the near-IR water combination band (about 10 500 cm-1) peak area is followed against added water until it plateaus at saturation.
uncertainties_stated: Temperature controlled to +-0.5 C; pressure +-1 bar; estimated error of the saturation concentration +-3 %.
quality_remarks: Only two in-scope values (water in CO2 at 50 and 75 C, 344.8 bar), in agreement with literature values quoted by the authors (0.75 and 1.35 mol %). Temperature scale not stated.
not_extracted_tables: Table 1 (physical data of solvents and water): physical properties, not measured solubility
Table 2 (water band positions and bandwidths): spectroscopic data
Table 4 (solubility of water in refrigerant 134a): system without in-scope gas

row_counts.Table 3: 6 printed, 6 written (2 CO2 rows in scope; R22/R134a rows in skip_rows)

extraction_notes: Pressure unit bar printed. Table 3 footnote letters b and c stripped from numbers and recorded in the note column.
